description.p: Caret is a terminal for Wayland. It draws its window and its text with Vulkan, pixel for pixel at any display scale.

ul.li: Tabs and split panes, and new tabs and windows in the folder of the current one
Sessions whose programs go on running while no window shows them, and windows that show several
Search through the history, selection by word or line, and addresses opened with Ctrl and a click
Mouse reporting, bracketed paste, true colour, and underline styles
The desktop's monospace font and colour scheme, or ones of its own

description.p: A tab moved to another session shown in the same window no longer stops updating.

ul.li: A window opened on a dark desktop no longer flashes light while the settings portal starts, as for the first window after login
The header bar and the terminal change together when the style switches between light and dark

description.p: Fixes for closing, copying and drawing.

ul.li: Closing a tab, a pane or a window asks first when it would end a program the tab was started with, or a job stopped or running in the background
Closing a window leaves running the sessions another window or caret session attach shows
Closing several tabs in quick succession closes all of them
A scroll bar set to show on hover shows only with the pointer on it
Programs can copy to the clipboard in a window before any key or click in it
New windows open after an update replaced Caret
A window keeps drawing after the GPU is reset or lost, as after a suspend
caret session attach takes a paste as one paste, and no longer types out mouse reports cut in two
The window size is kept when windows close together, as at logout
Saving a layout no longer freezes every terminal while a program is stuck on an unresponsive file system

description.p: Caret is written anew: programs run in a background server and output goes through a terminal emulator of its own, drawn with Vulkan and without GTK. It needs a Wayland compositor and a Vulkan 1.3 driver. Settings move to config.toml and start from the defaults.

ul.li: Programs keep running after a window is detached, and can be attached to again from another window, over ssh or from a console
Sessions: several can be shown in one window, named, given a colour, listed, and managed with caret session
Tabs split into panes, which can be swapped, moved, resized and zoomed by key and mouse; split presets lay out a tab from a file
Settings, colour schemes and presets are files that apply as soon as they are saved, and any key can be rebound
Scrolling moves by the pixel, with a scroll bar along each pane and a setting for how fast the wheel and the touchpad go
Text stays sharp at fractional scales
Scrolling, clicking and menus work with a finger, screen readers are told what the window shows, and shell completions are included
Ctrl+Shift+W closes the pane rather than the tab, which close-tab in the settings can bind, and Ctrl+Shift+O splits the pane rather than showing all tabs

description.p: Tangent is now called Caret. Its settings start from the defaults.

ul.li: New tabs open in the folder of the current one, and in its Toolbox or Distrobox container, where the shell reports them
Tabs show a running command, and a finished one or a notification in a tab that is not in view; Ctrl+Shift+Up and Down scroll between prompts
Tabs can be renamed from their context menu
The title bar can be hidden, and is in full screen
Selecting with the mouse scrolls past the edge; Select All and Deselect
The link under the pointer is underlined, and one a program broke into lines is followed
Symbols the font joins, such as -> and !=, are drawn joined, and a setting turns features of the font on and off
Settings for a command to run instead of the shell and for scrolling on output and on keystroke
Pasting several lines asks first where they would run, and programs can be kept from notifying and from copying
